identity.name: Taifa of Saltés and Huelva
alt_names: Taifa Kingdom of Saltés and Huelva

land.text: the coast around Saltés and Huelva

predecessors.note: The infobox says 'Preceded by: Taifa of Badajoz'; the Caliphate dossier hands the land over in 1012.

land.text: the whole first taifa, taken in 1051

successors.note: First period ends 1051; Seville held it to 1091.

land.text: the second taifa (unverified), ended by the Almohads

successors.note: Dates unverified: the Tejada page has the neighbouring taifa conquered by the Almohads in 1150.

capitals.name: Saltés (Huelva)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Saltés', the island at the mouth of the Odiel just south of Huelva; drawn at Huelva's coordinates because the gazetteer has no Saltés. Drawn 1012-1051 and 1147-1151 only.

rulers.name: 'Abd al-'Aziz 'Izz ad-Dawla
rulers.note: Bakrid dynasty; the page gives '1012/3–1051/2 or 53', the only ruler it lists.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox says 'Established: 1012' and the Taifa list '1012/1013–1051/1053 (Bakrid Dynasty)'; Cliopatria's first shape starts in 1015. The 1015 shape is applied back to 1012 (confidence 1 on the extent).
4,223 km2 on the Huelva coast between the Tinto-Odiel estuary and the Portuguese border. The infobox gives no area and the page names no boundary, so only size and bbox were checked.
4,149 km2, a 2 percent change from 1015 that no page explains (page silent); kept.

4,445 km2. The first taifa ends in 1051, not 1055: infobox 'Conquered by Seville: 1051'; 'From 1051 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of Seville'; the Abbad II page has 'Huelva (1051)'. The shape stands for 1028-1050.

4,223 km2, exactly the 1015 shape. Unverified: page silent. Neither the Saltés and Huelva page (which says nothing after 1091) nor the Taifa article's second-period list has a Saltés and Huelva; the Taifa of Tejada page puts a second-period taifa 'in the Province of Huelva', established 1146 and conquered by the Almohads in 1150, which may be what Cliopatria draws here.

region.text: the coast around Saltés and Huelva

ledger.note: 1012: the Bakrid taifa of Saltés and Huelva breaks away from the Caliphate of Córdoba. Infobox 'Established: 1012'; the ruler 'Abd al-'Aziz 'Izz ad-Dawla '1012/3–1051/2 or 53'; the page says the kingdom existed 'from around 1012 to 1051'. The page names the capital, not a boundary.
1051: Seville conquers Saltés and Huelva. Infobox 'Conquered by Seville: 1051'; 'From 1051 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of Seville, by Abbad II al-Mu'tadid.'

region.text: the coast around Saltés and Huelva, as Cliopatria draws it

ledger.note: 1147: a second Taifa of Saltés and Huelva appears in Cliopatria. Page silent on Saltés and Huelva; the Tejada page dates a second-period taifa in the Province of Huelva to 1146, so the Almoravid state is named as the land's previous holder.

1151: the second taifa ends, taken by the Almohads. Page silent on Saltés and Huelva: the Tejada page has 'Conquered by the Almohad Caliphate: 1150' for its neighbour and the Almohad dossier carries a gain from this taifa in 1152; Cliopatria's last shape is 1151.

wars.name: Abbadid conquest of Saltés and Huelva
wars.outcome: Seville conquered the taifa in 1051 and held it to 1091.
wars.note: The page names no battle; the Abbad II page lists 'Huelva (1051)' among al-Mu'tadid's conquests.

certainty.note: The pages give the capital and the taifa's name only; the estuary coast is firm, the inland frontier with Badajoz and Niebla approximate.

sources.title: Taifa of Saltés and Huelva
sources.note: Identity: established 1012, Bakrid ruler, capital Saltés, conquered by Seville 1051, silent after 1091.

sources.title: Taifa
sources.note: First-period list 'Saltés and Huelva: 1012/1013–1051/1053 (Bakrid Dynasty); 1051–1091 (to Seville)'; second-period list silent.

sources.title: Taifa of Tejada
sources.note: Second-period taifa in Huelva province 1146-1150; silent on Saltés and Huelva.

notes: (1) First period 1012-1051 is well sourced; the second period (Cliopatria 1147-1151, same geometry as 1015) is not on any page opened: the Saltés and Huelva page is silent after 1091 and the Taifa article lists no second taifa here; the Tejada page (1146-1150, Huelva province) and the Niebla page (1145-1150) may be the real second-period states. The Almohad dossier carries a conf-1 gain from this taifa in 1152. (2) The infobox says 'Preceded by: Taifa of Badajoz' while the Caliphate dossier hands the land over in 1012; the two are not reconciled. (3) Saltés is not in the gazetteer (capital placed at Huelva). (4) The infobox gives no area; shapes compared by size only.
